name: MI-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -15 point partisan lean
Incumbent John Moolenaar running with a $1.9 million war chest
Challenger Ben Ambrose raised only $85K with no outside support
model.rationale: Moolenaar is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 15 points, while Ambrose has raised under $100K and drawn no outside spending or expert attention. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Republican hold.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpectedly strong Democratic wave environment could narrow the margin, though an upset remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This is a heavily Republican district in central Michigan, where John Moolenaar is seeking another term as the incumbent. The partisan lean of the seat is roughly 15 points toward Republicans, and Moolenaar enters the race with about $1.9 million on hand after raising $1.65 million. No outside groups are spending against him, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Democratic challenger Ben Ambrose has raised about $85,000 with modest cash on hand, and no independent expenditure has materialized on either side. Prediction markets give Moolenaar roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. With no public polling available, the picture rests on fundamentals, all of which favor the incumbent by a wide margin.
